warnings: No customer corpus, interview, win/loss, CRM or on-site search evidence was supplied. Every ICP below is a public-evidence hypothesis, not a validated segment.
No age, income, title, household size, practice headcount or buying-committee composition has been invented. Fields without evidence are null.
icp-004 and icp-005 rest on company assertion or a weak search proxy only and are hypothesis_only. They may not enter core without human promotion plus new evidence.
Counterevidence is retained: source-005 (BBB, 4.89/5) and source-004 (ComplaintsBoard) describe the same service in opposite terms. Both are self-selected. Neither is prevalence.

standing_claims.text: The target operates a US marketplace where care-seekers filter providers by insurance, location, specialty and availability and book a real appointment slot.
Booking is free to the care-seeker; practices pay a one-time fee when a NEW patient books, varying by specialty and location.
The fee is charged at booking and is not automatically voided by a cancellation or no-show, though a 24-hour good-faith waiver and a 7-day existing-patient claim process exist.
The target self-reports 250k+ providers, 200+ specialties, 175+ EHR/PMS integrations and 50-state coverage.
Booking capability is being distributed onto third-party consumer surfaces, including a Yelp integration launched 2026-04-21 exposing real-time in-network availability.

icps.label: US insured care-seeker who must find a provider that is genuinely in-network, near enough, and available soon

context.situation: Needs a new provider (primary care, dental, or a specialty) and is constrained simultaneously by plan network, location and appointment availability rather than by any one of them

triggers.text: Relocation or plan change forces a new provider search from scratch
A provider listed as in-network turns out not to be, or the office has no record of the booking
A confirmed appointment is cancelled shortly before the visit

roles.label: same person; pays nothing to the marketplace but bears out-of-network cost risk
practice front desk that contradicts the listing

constraints.text: Must be in-network under a named plan; out-of-network exposure is the feared outcome
Availability window matters as much as fit
Directory information cannot be trusted without a second confirmation

disqualifiers.text: Emergency or acute clinical need requiring urgent/emergency care rather than scheduled booking

open_questions: Which specialties dominate real demand? The target claims 200+ (source-002) but only dental, primary care and mental health appear in independent or buyer evidence.
How often does the in-network mismatch actually occur on this marketplace specifically, as opposed to across US directories generally?

icps.label: US care-seeker trying to reach a mental-health provider through directories that are stale and networks that are effectively closed

context.situation: Working a plan directory or list of therapists where listings are unreachable, full, or not actually in-network, while holding a job that makes repeated daytime calling difficult

triggers.text: Repeated unreturned calls and full voicemail boxes when working a directory list
Directory contact details are out of date
Providers who are listed are not accepting new patients

constraints.text: Limited time to make repeated follow-up calls during business hours
Insurance coverage is a hard requirement, not a preference

disqualifiers.text: Crisis or acute-risk situations, which are out of scope for a marketing measurement panel

open_questions: source-012 is verbatim but dated 2021-07-19. Has this language shifted? Fresh forum evidence is needed at the next refresh.
source-011 measured Medicare Advantage directories, not this marketplace. Does the marketplace's availability data materially outperform plan directories? No independent test was found.

icps.label: US independent or small-group practice owner buying new-patient volume and judging it on cost per acquired patient

context.unit: solo or small-group practice (dental, mental health, primary care evidenced)
context.situation: Has unfilled schedule capacity, pays a per-new-patient fee for marketplace bookings, and cannot easily predict or control the monthly total

triggers.text: Schedule capacity is unfilled and the owner must decide where to buy new patients
A per-booking charge lands for a patient who cancelled or did not show
A returning patient is billed as a new-patient acquisition
Fee levels are not visible until late in sign-up and vary by specialty and market

roles.label: owner-clinician who signs off on acquisition spend
practice operations / front-desk manager who runs the schedule and the billing disputes
same owner evaluating retention and blended cost after several months

constraints.text: Per-new-patient fee cited between roughly $35 and $110 depending on specialty and market
Fee applies whether or not the patient attends
Decision is benchmarked on blended cost per new patient across all channels, not on one channel's price
New-patient lifetime value is the denominator the owner must estimate first

open_questions: The two richest sources on the provider decision (source-007, source-008) are published by competing vendors. An unaffiliated practice-owner survey or an association source is needed before any fee figure is treated as fact.
source-003 records that provider counts reportedly rose 50% after the per-booking transition, which sits against the owner-complaint evidence. Both are retained; neither is resolved.

icps.label: Multi-location group, health system or DSO evaluating patient-access and scheduling infrastructure

context.situation: Evaluating EHR-integrated scheduling, call deflection and distributed booking across many locations

triggers.text: Inbound scheduling calls exceed staff capacity, including after hours

constraints.text: Requires integration with existing EHR/PMS systems

open_questions: Every element of this ICP comes from the target's own provider page. No independent source, buyer-language source, procurement guide or analyst source describing this buying context was found.

Evidence needed to promote: an independent case study, an RFP or procurement document, or health-system practitioner discussion. Until then this ICP supports one quarantined rotating cell and nothing in core.

icps.label: US self-pay or uninsured care-seeker who needs a price before committing to a booking

context.situation: Booking without usable insurance coverage and needing the visit cost up front
context.coverage_status: uninsured or paying out of pocket

triggers.text: Needs same-day or near-term care without a usable plan, and searches surface self-pay telehealth and no-referral booking options
A booking made as self-pay conflicts with insurance information presented at the visit

constraints.text: Price transparency before booking is the binding requirement

open_questions: The only support is search-result composition (source-013), which is a proxy for what publishers target, not for what care-seekers ask. No forum, review or verbatim source was found.

The target's stated organising axis is insurance, which may make this segment structurally out of scope rather than under-served. Evidence needed: buyer-language sources from self-pay care-seekers, or a target-side self-pay capability page.

excluded_contexts.reason: Target coverage claimed as 50 US states only

excluded_contexts.label: Payer / employer benefits procurement
excluded_contexts.reason: No evidence found in this run

excluded_contexts.label: Caregiver booking on behalf of a dependent or older adult
excluded_contexts.reason: Plausible and probably material, but no evidence source was found. Recorded as a research gap rather than an invented role.

open_research_questions: The supplied URL (target homepage) returned HTTP 403 to the fetch agent. Direct capture of the patient-side product surface, its specialty taxonomy and its stated locale support is outstanding.
No lawfully collected AI-conversation evidence exists for this category. All prompt language is reconstructed from reviews, one forum thread and search proxies.
No Spanish-language evidence was found despite the US market. This is an unresolved coverage gap, not a decision that the segment does not exist.
